state.objective: The requested endpoint is native Can ownership of every test and its coordinating code in /tests; the user chose removal of Go/TS host harnesses as well. We are only studying the migration now. Compiler code in Go and platform machinery in Bun can remain, but disguising existing test procedures as platform functions would fail the request.
state.capabilities: Available Can mechanisms include functions with required asserts, per-call when FIFO fixtures, scenarios/templates, checks::require, JSON conversion, filesystem calls and process::run. A child execution yields separate output streams plus status/signal, with cwd, environment, input, deadline and byte caps specified. Effects work from normal main execution, whereas attached assertions prohibit live boundaries. There is no language-wide finally. Native owned resources have scope cleanup, with no cleanup guarantee after forced process death.
state.runner: The assert command validates an entire project before narrowing roots, supervises independent workers using --assert-jobs and deadlines, and emits a JSON report. The run command first verifies assertions and publishes a build, then invokes main. Can currently lacks a repository-wide integration case registry/scheduler/report interface. Invalid code can be staged in distinct projects and judged by subprocess failure/diagnostic text. A structured semantic-check CLI would need adding, though a diagnostics API already exists.
state.gaps: The implemented process primitive completes only when its child exits; clients cannot obtain a continuing child handle, arrange arbitrary inherited descriptors or send chosen signals. Existing suites exercise credential fd 3, orderly stops and crashes, restarts, ports, temporary directories and orphan recovery. Normal HTTP inspection already fits named fetch http::response<bytes::buffer>, which returns status, normalized headers and bytes. Precise malformed requests, trickled data and connection interruption require additional low-level operations.
state.browser: The browser catalogue controls DOM inside an app rather than an external browser session. Playwright-based suites currently drive Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, including page navigation, input events, interception, console and DOM readings, and adversarial boundary behavior. Native conformance also manipulates or observes Bun features such as proxies and thenables that Can-safe values cannot construct. Preserving these oracles means acquiring independent observations, not merely round-tripping through the same adapter under examination.
state.constraints: Backward compatibility is unnecessary because no external users exist; behavioral evidence matters more than retaining old test shapes or totals. A 256 GB laptop constrains storage/load: avoid broad qualification, measurements, enduring private caches and copied dependencies. Share the candidate artifact within each run, cap concurrency/durations/output, and establish cleanup on allocation. Some tracked /tests content is fixture data or archived evidence. A compiler under test may also break the runner it compiles; retaining a verified runner binary separates that risk at the price of intentional artifact maintenance.

execution.instructions: Select the most suitable initial implementation route for replacing the foreign-language harness completely without weakening offline assertion semantics or adding needless syntax. This is a prototype recommendation, not a statement of present support.

criteria.suite_program: Build the suite as an ordinary Can executable whose main orchestrates function cases through current process, file, codec and check APIs. Supply missing generic resource/observation facilities, exercise runner logic with deterministic asserts, and optionally front it later with canlc test.
criteria.live_assertions: Introduce opt-in live assertion execution while leaving existing assertions deterministic. Teach selection, supervision and reports about the live class, keeping it out of default verified builds and keeping coordination rules in Can.
criteria.test_declarations: Design a separate native testing declaration construct for discoverable cases and suite lifetime. Leave current asserts alone and implement coordinating behavior in Can on top of platform capabilities.
criteria.undetermined: Postpone choosing a route because a material missing fact needs a narrowly scoped investigation.

browser.instructions: What should the next browser-architecture investigation prioritize if cases and pass/fail decisions must be Can source and real behavior on all current engines must remain observable?

criteria.typed_driver: Add closed typed automation calls that delegate to upstream Playwright through maintained platform implementations. Return measurements and events to Can, where scenario flow and checks live; no adapter function may encode a former whole test.
criteria.can_protocol: Write a Can client for upstream browser-driver protocols using HTTP/WebSocket and managed child processes. Establish feature parity per engine and take responsibility for the larger protocol implementation.
criteria.capability_spike: Try the demanding browser interactions in a limited evidence-gathering spike, comparing the two integration mechanisms before committing to either.

bootstrap.instructions: Choose a normal trust model for a Can-written compiler integration runner that balances correlated compiler failures against bounded execution cost.

criteria.known_good: Drive the candidate and inspect its artifacts with a hash-identified runner built by a previously verified compiler; keep fixed independent vectors and refresh that runner through explicit review.
criteria.candidate_only: Compile the runner only with the candidate, supplementing it with deliberately failing controls, literal expected data and the independent compiler/runtime unit coverage located outside /tests.
criteria.dual: Run both previously verified and newly candidate-compiled versions of the suite each time, comparing results while accepting the extra work and resource use.
